docs/phase-7-routing/sprint2_ar3_context_windows.json v1.0.0 (classification model and per-story context-window method reused verbatim from Sprint 2; not re-derived)
methodology_reuse_note: Same per-story context-window design method as sprint2_ar3_context_windows.json: sources are the exact HLD section / SRS-AC / backlog-note / AR1 must-not-deviate citations the story's own routing record names, never invented additions. context_budget_tokens is a judgment call scaled to how much real source content (HLD prose + endpoint tables + ADR text, ACs, must_not_deviate items, cross-references) the story actually cites, following the same 3500-7000 band Sprint 1/2 used, not a fixed formula. Sprint 3 differs from Sprint 1/2 in one respect: two stories (DASH-STORY-023, DASH-STORY-024) do not touch zone content or PII at all, but do touch a materially new class of sensitive material (real network exposure, real adapter credentials) that the classification model's Bell-LaPadula PII ceiling was never written to cover. That new class is flagged explicitly per classification_model.sprint_3_new_risk_class_note below, and each affected story's context window is scoped the same way a PII-ceiling story's would be: structural/contract shape admitted, no real secret or credential value ever included.

classification_model.name: Bell-LaPadula classification-ceiling (carried forward unchanged from ar3_context_windows.json / sprint2_ar3_context_windows.json)
classification_model.rule: No story's context window may include Zone 2 (Episodic) or Zone 5 (Entity) content bearing PII unless the story itself is security-cleared. No Sprint 3 story is security-cleared for raw PII read access. Where a story's implementation reasoning needs to reference Zone 2/5 content shape, a redacted/pseudonymized synthetic example is substituted for any real or realistic PII value.
classification_model.zone_3_extension_note: Carried forward unchanged from sprint2_ar3_context_windows.json: Zone 3 (Semantic) is not itself named in the ceiling rule, but its relationship-fact content (SemanticEdge subject_ref/predicate/object_ref) is treated with the same redaction caution as a Zone 2/5-adjacent zone for any story whose decisive content is real fact content rather than structural/contract shape.
classification_model.zone_8_extension_note: Carried forward unchanged: Zone 8 (Consolidation) holds the longest-lived PII per ADR-009's India Layer text and is treated with ceiling-equivalent discipline even though the rule's literal text names only Zones 2 and 5.
classification_model.sprint_3_new_risk_class_note: DASH-STORY-023 (FR-014, the wire/API layer) and DASH-STORY-024 (FR-015, Shape B deployment infrastructure) are the first two stories in any sprint that trigger a security-relevant exclusion for a reason OTHER than zone-content PII: HLD Section 10's asset list names 'adapter credentials' as asset (5), on the same sensitivity list as memory payloads and embeddings, and sprint3_ar1_assignments.json's own routing_gaps entry AR1-S3-G3 explicitly discloses that DASH-STORY-023 is 'the first real network-facing host application this codebase has ever had' and DASH-STORY-024 is 'where real, non-default DB/object-store credentials go live for the first time' - genuine security-relevant firsts that do not fire any of the three literal p1_security_override criteria (Zone 7 touch, ZoneRepository port change, cross-tenant isolation logic) and so are carried only as non-blocking advisory reviews (api-security-auditor, cloud-security-architect), not P1 gates. This context-window file applies the same discipline to that risk class that the Bell-LaPadula rule applies to PII: the implementing agent's context window admits the CONTRACT (signing-key fail-closed behavior, credential-sourced-from-env requirement, mTLS+JWT tenant-binding shape, service port/protocol table) and never an actual secret, key, or connection-string value - there being no real value to redact yet, since neither story has shipped.

context_windows.title: FR-011 zone-coverage closure: verify pluggable-storage-adapter substitutability holds across Zone 3 and Zone 5's Sprint-2 adapters
context_windows.pii_note: This story runs a shared ZoneRepository-port contract-test suite against Zone 3 (SqlSemanticRepository) and Zone 5 (EntityMemoryRepository)'s already-shipped adapters. Per the classification model, Zone 5 is a ceiling zone and Zone 3's relationship-fact content is treated with equivalent caution. Unlike DASH-STORY-012/013 (Sprint 2), this story's own acceptance criteria (AC-021-1) require only that the contract suite pass 'with zero adapter-specific behavioral leakage' - a structural, port-shape assertion, not a fact-content assertion. The context window therefore admits the port contract and the adapter file list, and requires only synthetic/placeholder fixture data for the contract-test seed rows, never a real or illustrative-realistic entity/attribute value; the HLD's own Sachin/Mumbai worked example is not needed here since this story does not touch EntityOwnershipSpecification's routing logic (that is DASH-STORY-013's closed Sprint 2 scope, not this story's).
context_windows.assigned_agent_note: Synced 2026-09-20 per SP3-DEC-106 (see sprint3_ar1_assignments.json's DASH-STORY-021.assigned_agent_note): reassigned from python-backend-engineer to api-testing-engineer. Previously unsynced -- flagged and fixed after external review.

context_windows.title: Wire the existing FR-013 conflict-detection sweep into the real Zone 3 and Zone 5 write paths
context_windows.pii_note: This story routes two existing Zone 3/Zone 5 write call sites through the existing, already-tested ConflictDetectingProvenanceRepository decorator. The context window carries the routing/algorithm CONTRACT (which fields determine a contradiction match - (entity, predicate) or (subject, predicate, object) - and the -0.3 disputed-confidence modifier from HLD Section 3.8) but no real or realistic fact content: the acceptance criteria (AC-022-1/2) are themselves written in terms of abstract (entity, predicate)/(subject, predicate, object) placeholders, not example values, so no HLD worked-example substitution was needed here the way DASH-STORY-012/013 required one in Sprint 2. domain/conflict_detection.py's own algorithm is explicitly out of scope (must_not_deviate) and is not included in this context window beyond the confidence-modifier constant already public in HLD Section 3.8.

context_windows.pii_note: This spike is documentation/dependency research only (Qdrant client-version x server-version x Python-3.12+ compatibility matrix) - it touches no zone, no zone adapter, and no zone content at all, the same posture ar3_context_windows.json and sprint2_ar3_context_windows.json gave to non-ceiling, non-zone-touching stories (e.g. Sprint 2's DASH-STORY-015/016). No redaction was required or applicable.

context_windows.title: Wire/API layer: real FastAPI/gRPC host implementing the existing openapi.yaml contract, closing DSHN-60
context_windows.pii_note: Security_surface_note (new risk class per classification_model.sprint_3_new_risk_class_note): this story is the codebase's first real network-facing host application. Two distinct exclusions apply. (1) PII-shape exclusion, standard ceiling discipline: the 32 wired endpoints (assembleContext, writeMemory, eraseSubject, etc.) carry request/response payload FIELDS that may contain conversational PII per HLD Section 10 asset (1); this context window admits only the operationId/field-shape contract (openapi.yaml's own schema names) and composition_root.py's fail-closed signing-key verification logic (load_tenant_credential_signing_key_from_env), never an example payload value or a real memory item's content. (2) Credential/network-surface exclusion, the new risk class: this is the first story where a real, network-reachable host exists at all; the context window carries the mTLS+JWT tenant-binding CONTRACT and the 'must construct every orchestrator/repository instance through composition_root.py, never a bare constructor call' rule, but no actual signing-key value, certificate, or connection detail, since none exists yet at this stage. The api-security-auditor advisory review (SP3-DEC-102) runs in its own separate review context per sprint3_ar1_assignments.json and is not folded into this implementer's context window.

context_windows.title: Shape B deployment infrastructure: Postgres/Redis/Qdrant/OpenSearch/S3, docker-compose, env config, migration runner
context_windows.pii_note: Security_surface_note (new risk class per classification_model.sprint_3_new_risk_class_note): this is the story where dashanan_provenance_role/dashanan_episodic_role/dashanan_schema_owner (the real, current role names defined in provenance_schema.sql/episodic_schema.sql since the DSHN-60 P1 remediation - corrected from sprint3_ar1_assignments.json's own AC-024-2 fix of backlog_draft.json's stale 'dashanan_app_role' citation) get bound to a real, non-default login credential for the first time, and where Postgres/Redis/Qdrant/OpenSearch/S3 become real, network-reachable services for the first time - per HLD Section 10 asset (5) 'adapter credentials' and ADR-009's India Layer text ('Zone 8 holds the longest-lived PII', per-subject keys must be individually destroyable). This context window admits only the credential-binding CONTRACT (env-config sourcing, never a hardcoded value, per AC-024-2) and the five services' documented port/protocol shape (AC-024-1), never any actual generated password, connection string, or key material - none exists yet since the story has not shipped. The cloud-security-architect advisory review (SP3-DEC-104) runs in its own separate review context and is not folded into this implementer's context window.

context_windows.title: DPDP erasure-cascade reach into Zone 3 (Semantic) and Zone 5 (Entity) data (DSHN-70)
context_windows.pii_note: The most direct PII/DPDP story in Sprint 3, alongside DASH-STORY-023's network-surface disclosure. Its subject matter is the erasure reach into Zone 3 (SemanticEdge.subject_ref) and Zone 5 (EntityRecord attributes keyed by entity_id) for a given subject_id. Same strictest-redaction discipline sprint2_ar3_context_windows.json applied to DASH-STORY-017 (direct Zone 5 activation) and DASH-STORY-020 (Zone 8 crypto-shredding key lifecycle): this context window carries the erasure CONTRACT (subject_id/entity_id-keyed delete/state-transition path, the zone_4_exclusion rationale that Procedure carries no subject-linkable field, and SRS Section 4.1's own docs-drift disclosure that the currently shipped mechanism is a plain DELETE/eviction, not crypto-shredding) but never any real or example subject_id, entity attribute value, or SemanticEdge/GeneralFact content. AC-013's still-open crypto-shredding-mechanism gap and OAQ-10's still-open legal question are both carried forward as explicitly open, never asserted as resolved by this story. The crypto-security-specialist advisory review (SP3-DEC-105) runs in its own separate review context and is not folded into this implementer's context window.

summary.strictest_redaction: DASH-STORY-025 (direct Zone 3/5 DPDP erasure-cascade reach) carries the strictest content-redaction discipline, the same class Sprint 2 gave DASH-STORY-017 and DASH-STORY-020. DASH-STORY-023 and DASH-STORY-024 carry an equivalent-strictness discipline for a different reason: neither touches zone content directly, but both are flagged per classification_model.sprint_3_new_risk_class_note as the codebase's first real network-facing host (023) and first real production DB/object-store credentials (024) - a risk class the Bell-LaPadula PII ceiling was not written to cover, and which sprint3_ar1_assignments.json's own routing_gaps entry AR1-S3-G3 discloses does not fire any literal p1_security_override criterion.
summary.note_on_security_clearance: No Sprint 3 story is security-cleared for raw PII or for provisioning real production credentials, matching Sprint 1/2's posture. DASH-STORY-022's crypto-security-specialist advisory review (SP3-DEC-101), DASH-STORY-023's api-security-auditor advisory review (SP3-DEC-102), DASH-STORY-024's cloud-security-architect advisory review (SP3-DEC-104), and DASH-STORY-025's crypto-security-specialist advisory review (SP3-DEC-105) each operate in their own separate review context per sprint3_ar1_assignments.json - none of that reviewer-level access is granted to, or folded into, the implementing agents' (python-backend-engineer / devops-engineer / ai-engineer) context windows documented here. All four advisory reviews remain OPEN and not yet accepted by the user as of this file's date.
